title: Nuclear emulsions record cosmic-ray 'stars'
summary: Marietta Blau developed photographic emulsions to track high-energy particles and, with Hertha Wambacher, found 'disintegration stars' from cosmic rays.
why: A key tool of early particle physics.

unsung.contribution: Developed photographic nuclear emulsions for imaging particles and found cosmic-ray disintegration stars.
unsung.recognition: Cecil Powell won the 1950 Nobel Prize for work partly built on hers; she was never awarded one.
